subject.title: feat(dashboard): pinned MCP apps — board rendering, lease re-mint, durable tool grants

question: Should the initial pinned-MCP-app design enforce a board-visible lease limit or introduce a lifecycle that prevents mounted widgets from evicting one another from the shared 32-view lease store?
rationale: The required repair affects the intended V1 dashboard behavior and resource-ownership model; the evidence establishes the mismatch but not which product constraint maintainers want to preserve.

options.title: Require bounded mounted leases
options.body: Block rendering or defer inactive widgets so no mounted board can exceed the shared live-view capacity.

options.title: Make lease ownership board-aware
options.body: Change the lease lifecycle or capacity model so all simultaneously mounted board widgets can remain valid without evicting one another.

options.title: Accept a documented V1 cap
options.body: Keep the shared cap only if the UI clearly limits pins or mounted widgets and explains the constraint before users encounter evictions.

recommendation.title: Make lease ownership board-aware
recommendation.body: Change the lease lifecycle or capacity model so all simultaneously mounted board widgets can remain valid without evicting one another.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch establishes the dashboard widget and lease-reconstruction design that needs an explicit capacity decision.
